texts.preamble: Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 In The Court Of The Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court - Iv, Bangalore Present: Gayathri.S.Kate, B.com, Llb., Mmtc - Iv, Bangalore Dated : This The 3Rd Day Of January 2018 Crl.Misc.No.21/2011 Petitioner: Smt. R. Chandana, Age: 27 years, D/o. M. Ramaswamy, R/at No.94, 4th cross, B.C.C. Layout, Chandra Layout, Vijayanagara 2nd stage, Bangalore - 560 040 Vs. Respondent: 1)Sri H. Manjunath, Age: 35 years, S/o. K. Hanumanthappa, R/at 'A', 207, Vijay Vihar Powai, Mumbai - 400 076 And also at No.3, Priyadarshini Estate, Pillaganahalli cross, Gottigere Post, Bannerughatta Road, Bangalore south - 560 083
texts.facts: This is a petition filed by the petitioner U/s.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 seeking relief's U/s.18, 19, 20 and 22 of the said Act. 2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that the marriage proposal of the respondent No.1 came through one Mr. K.V. Devanath i.e., her father's colleague. Her parents had proceeded to arrange her marriage with the respondent who, she had her family members were given to understand was working as an educational consultant at Mumbabi. She state that initially, the respondents themselves had insisted that the marriage be performed in a simple manner in accordance with Hindu Customs in Dharmasthala by exchange of garlands by both the petitioner and the respondent in front of Lord Manjunatha Swamy in the presence of only the family of both the petitioner and the respondents. The marriage proposal was dragged on by the respondents for nearly 16 months after the introduction by Shri K.V. Devanath. However, after the initial agreement for marriage between the petitioner and the respondent, the respondent No.2 and 3 changed their version by demanding a grand engagement ceremony to be performed in a reputed hotel and later to host a grand reception in Bangalore at a five star hotel and also at Mumbai at a seven star hotel. The entire marriage expenses of the petitioner are borne by my father. This was apart from the demands for ornaments, garments and other paraphernalia is to be given after the marriage. Though her parents were only prepared for performing a moderate marriage, based on the demands which were initially spoken by the respondent No.2 and 3, they had also alternative but to accede to their demands because of the prolonged rapport of marriage alliance between both the families i.e., for nearly 16 months, everyone in the society had become aware that my marriage will only be performed with the respondent No.1. She state that her parents and she however requested the respondent No.1 to 3 that we will perform the engagement and the reception at Bangalore as per their wish and also give whatever they had told to her after the marriage. Hence, with only moderate financial resource and also keeping in mind that two more sisters whose education and marriage had to be taken into account, her parents struggled to accumulate financial resources to meet the demands set forth by them. Her parents were forced to agree to the demands Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141608679/ 2 happiness after marriage as well as the future of her two unmarried sisters. Also their whole family, and their friends were impressed by the respondent No.1's attitude and behaviour which he had posed during the 16 months of interaction with her and her family members before the marriage. She states that the betrothal ceremony was performed in Nandini Deluxe hotel, Bangalore on 27-01-2008 after which the marriage was performed in Hindu Tradition in Dharmasthala in front of Lord Manjunatha swamy by exchange of Garlands on 10-03-2008 which was followed by a grand reception in Hotel Ashok at Bangalore on 12-03-2008 as per the wishes and demands of respondents. The other materialistic demands were complied and sent along with her, when she went to her martial house to begin her newly married life. The only wish and demands which was not fulfilled was hosting a reception at a seven star hotel at Mumbai, which her parents had already informed them in advance that it was beyond the means, capabilities and financial resources of her father and other relatives and also was to be arranged by them at their own cost if they so desired to have a reception in Mumbai, since a reception was already performed in Bangalore at her parents' expenses. She state that the engagement, marriage and reception was organized in an excellent manner and went on very cordially and greatly enjoyed by both the families and also highly appreciated by all the relatives and well-wishers from both the families. She state that after the marriage, all formalities as per customs was completed by her family members and in all best possible manner and she was sent to the marital home in Bangalore on 13-03-2008 as Mrs. Chandana Manjunath along with jewelry, garments like silk sarees and regular attire and other paraphernalia as per their wish and demands. As the respondent No.1 was employed in Mumbai, she and the respondents left for Mumbai on 19-03-2008 where the respondent No.1 had his residence. She state that on reaching Mumbai, married life began to be a nightmare for her as she was tormented and taunted by respondents, who all kept on repeatedly shouting at her and her parents had not fulfilled their demand for hosting a reception at Mumbai. Adding to this, they placed new demands i.e., asking her to get from her parents a new SKODA car, a three bedroom flat at Mumbai and also a BDA site in a posh locality at Bangalore. They forced her to place these demands to her parents through telephone from Mumbai. On hearing their atrocious demands, her parents were taken a back. Knowing very well their background i.e., her father was working as a salaried person as Executive in a Public Sector with very little service left and also the added responsibility of getting two of her younger sisters married, it would be highly impossible to meet their demands which runs into crores of rupees which would be impossible to earn in a life time. Hence, her parents told her through telephone to gently explain their circumstances and also to explain to them that they had two more daughters whose education is still to be pursued and after which their marriage has also to be performed. She state that after she explained the circumstances to the respondents, the situation turned worse. She was abused in a wile manner and in foul languages by all respondent No.1 to 3 continuously, day-in and day-out that her parents were unable to even meet their demands. This abuse led to acute mental agony and harassment for her. Apart from this, she was totally restricted to even go out for getting anything to meet her Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141608679/ 3 personal needs. The respondent No.1, 2 and 3 even locked her up. She was forced to not only do all the menial jobs in their home for her in laws, but also was taken to respondent No.4's house in Mumbai where she was asked to do all the work like a maid servant. The respondent No.4 also used to abuse her a lot then calling her names and abusing her using very bad and foul language. She was never taken out by the respondent No.1 even to see any place in Mumbai or for any entertainment as a newly married couple. Even her food was restricted to only what they wanted her to eat and never used to give her proper food or in time. Even with all this torture and discomfort faced by her, she never once uttered her discomfort or displeasure to the respondent No.1, because she was brought up by her parents in a very disciplined manner according to their culture as how a Hindu woman should behave and also with the fond hope that they will all realize their follies and will start treating her with the least respect she deserve. She state that being a faithful and humble wife to respondent No.1, she took care of all the needs of respondent No.1 and out of respect took care of all the needs of the respondent No.2 and 3 as well. She state that at around that time she conceived. The respondent No.1 to 3 continued to taunt and torture her. She silently bore all the pains and put up with all their tantrums as a wife and daughter-in-law respectively. When the situation reached out of control to bear anymore atrocities caused by the respondent No.1 to 3, she was constrained to inform her parents who in turn advised her not to lose faith and endure the pain of torture and that all her problems will. She state that her parents brought her for her confinement to the house during the seventh month of her pregnancy. Before that, they performed seemantham for her in her parents house. They insisted that the delivery should be in the best hospital in Bangalore and a suite should be taken up in the hospital during delivery. They also demanded that the stem-cell of the child should be preserved in a reputed stem-cell preserving organization located at Gurgaon. According to their wish and demands, her parents had admitted her in the best hospital in a private suite for my delivery and a bonny daughter was born on 17-06-2009 who was named as Disha at the age of 11th month (19th April 2010). We also did the preservation of stem-cell of the child as per the wish and demands of the respondents. The entire medical pre and post delivery expenses were fully borne by her parents. She state that though she was in her parents' house two months prior to delivery and six months after delivery, the respondent No.1 hardly visited her and her child. Even the three to four times that the respondent No.1's visit to meet her and his child, instead of being joyous on becoming a father , he started telling her that he was not really interested in her, because prior to their marriage, he had an affair with a woman and since the respondent No.2 and 3 had objected to his affair, he was forced to marry her. This the respondent no1. told her during her stay in Mumbai and she was subjected to a lot of abuses by respondent No.1 when she asked him about this. He further went on to add fuel to fire by telling her that now he had further entanglement with other women and hardly felt her absence as he enjoyed the company of other women. He also went on to threaten her and he had ample money, he can enjoy his life with whomever he wanted to, and in case she gave him any hindrance in his activities, he would not hesitate to not only divorce her but also take Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141608679/ 4 away the child born not because he had any love towards the child but with the purpose of only harassing her and making her suffer. He further added that in case she divulged any of these to her parents, he would not hesitate in getting them murdered through his sources since he knew people from underworld in Mumbai. In order to prove all this was true, whenever he stayed in the privacy of their room, he used to make calls to the women, with whom he was carrying on relationship after the marriage in front of her causing her a lot of mental pain and harassment. This was really an agonizing experience to her, because she only revolved around his world and was taken aback to see the other side of his behaviour. Even knowing all this, she never once told her parents all these facts, with great faith and hope that he will change his ways for the better, as he sees his daughter growing up and also to up keep the family honour and name in the society. She state that during the respondent No.1's visits to meet her and the child, all her family members bestowed on him the highest respect as a respected son-in-law. In the meanwhile, the respondent No.1 also observed that her brother R. Naveen who had started a small business of his own was slowly coming up and got jealous of him and started keeping a track of his business activities unnecessarily which was during the marriage and before departure to Mumbai. During this time, her brother R. Naveen was in the process of seeking loans through several lending agencies for his business. Since her family members were unable to meet the respondents demands of hosting a reception in a seven star hotel in Mumbai he also started alleging to her, that he was approached by her father and brother for advancing Rs.50,00,000/- towards her brother's business. This is entirely contradictory by himself, as since her parents could not meet his demands for hosting a reception at Mumbabi, how on the contrary, could they ask him for any assistance for business. This allegation is utterly false and based on assumptions and imagination. Further, respondent's claim that her brother is an alcoholic and has rave parties is absurd baseless. Her brother is married and having a child of two years. He has been brought up in a very orthodox family background; he has sought to do his own business where he cam provide for his family. But the respondent No.1 is making allegations against her brother which are utterly baseless with the sole intention of causing trouble in his married life as well as cause untold misery to her. She state that on 20-10-2009, the respondent No.4 abused in a filthy language and also threatened her asking her to leave her marital home on her own or else she will throw her out of the house and she poured life threats to her. The respondent No.4 used to instigate the respondent No.1 to 3 to ill treat and harass her to get more dowry, and ordered them not to give food to her and throw her out of the house. During her pregnancy, the respondent No.4 also used to abuse her verbally and demanded stating that before her delivery she should not money from her parents to buy a plot in Bombay and also to buy a car for her brother. The respondent No.1 to 3 without condemning her verbal abuse and demanding behavior were only too happy to support her. At that time respondent No.1 to 3 never came to help her. Because of her involvement in her marital life and her instigation towards the respondent No.1 to 3 demand dowry from her parents, it only added fuel to the exiting the harassment. The situation became worse from bad. She also kept telling that she had some incurable disease which was totally false and she being a dental doctor, the respondent No.1-3 believed her and their abuse increased multi-fold due to that. All of them together caused her violence verbally, physically, mentally and also financially as they used to not give her any money even for her basic needs. She state that on 24th December 2009 late in the evening, the respondent Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141608679/ 5 No.1 visited her parents house and early morning on 25th December 2009, he packed up all her belongings and the child's, and without the knowledge of her parents took her and her child to his parent's house in Bangalore. Her family members were shocked and taken by utter surprise by his action and attitude, since there were many customs and procedures to be followed by both the families while sending the girl with her new born child back to her husband's house. Her parents tried contacting her by phone on 25th and 26th December 2009 which was not responded, as she was not allowed to take the call which caused her utmost mental torture caught between what the respondents were saying as well as the situation her parents were in. However, on the 27th December 2009, somehow, she was able to talk to her parents. As her family members tried to talk to her, she was pressurized by the respondents and had to tell them that they should forget her and not to contact her again. The respondent No.1 took the receiver from her and started abusing her father in unparliamentarily words like idiot, stupid, bastard etc., and told that he will teach her a lesson, if her father again tried to contact her and said that if her father had the guts to face him, he should go and meet him and cut of the conversation. This caused her a lot of mental hurt. On the same day, the respondent No.3 called up her home from her phone and gave it to her and forced her to inform her family members that they should not worry and that she was being safeguarded by them and that they need not come and meet her. This the respondent No.3 told was because he feared that matters were going bad in the house which may have a bad repercussions and so the respondent No.2 and 3 had left their house to stay in a relative's house to save themselves if her or her parents were forced to seek police help and intervention. She state that since her family members were not in peace of mind with all these incidents and fearing her safely in view of the acute violence meted out to her by the respondents, her parents called her up in the afternoon of 29th December 2009 to enquire about her well being. On taking her father's call, she started weeping and said "you all will not be able to see her again in your life and hence please forget her" and hung up the phone. This was due to the difficult time given by the respondent No.1 to her and instigated and supported in this by respondent No.2 to 4. On getting this response, her family members were worried as to what was happening in her life, and so her parents again called up after about 10 minutes and at this time the call was taken by the respondent No.1 who abused her father in very bad and filthy language and hung up the phone. She state that fearing that something adverse was happening to her and she was in danger, her parents, her brother, her uncles and aunt and her father's neighbour visited the respondents' house around 9.00 p.m. to plead with the respondent No.1 to 3, not to harass her and to take care of her and the child. Her parents came inside their house and were seated and started having a talk with the respondent No.2 to sort out any issues which they may not be aware of. All of a sudden, the respondent No.1 entered the living room where they were discussing and started abusing all of them in a very bad language stating that "how dare her family members entered his house without his permission" and that they should get out. Her parents meekly and politely asked him not to be aggressive and that they can sort out any issues by talking in fair and just manner politely. For this, the respondent No.1 rushed towards a wardrobe and opened it and got out a big Laathi (wooden stick) and started attacking her family members. Her father was injured in his hand, while her brother got injured in the forehead. Her parents had no alternative but to leave the house. Her parents and broher went to Bannerghatta police station closest to the residence of respondents No.2 and 3 and met head constable, who was night-in-charge, Shri Renuka Prasad and informed him of the incident in detail orally. He informed that if her parents gave a complaint in writing he will be in a position to initiate action. Since this Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141608679/ 6 was family issue which involved of her life, and with the hope that things will return to normalcy and that the respondents will realize their mistake and change for the better, her parents and her brother did not lodge any complaint and returned back to their house. She state that since her parents came to her matrimonial home and came to know of the real fact of how she was being treated there, in order to safeguard himself and his parents, the respondent No.1 wrote a complaint against her family members and forced her also to sign the same without even allowing her to read the contents. Even the respondent No.2 made a similar statement that he and his wife were in no way concerned with the activities or action being carried out by his son that is the 1st respondent and forced her to sign the same. She had no option but to sign the same. She state that after her parents' visit i.e., 29th December 2009, the physical and mental torture towards her continued and even escalated to a hgreater extent and on 31st December 2009, she was demeaned and forced by the respondent No.1 and 2 to go to her parents house and get an apology letter from her father so that they can teach him a lesson and then only the respondent No.1 will accept her as his wife and allow her to live with him. She telephoned to her parents who in turn sent her brother R. Naveen with a vehicle to bring her to parents' house. Her father was on duty in his place of work when she reached her parents' house. During this time, she narrated all the incidents of torture she had undergone from 25th December 2009 till she arrived on 31st December 2009 to her family members which shocked her parents that these people were capable of harassing her so much. She state that since the time she was taken to my in- laws house in Bangalore. she was physically tortured by the respondent No.1 and also verbally abused in the foulest language that she should sever all contact and relationship with her parents, brother and sisters. She also said that on 26th December 2009, her husband had bitten her all over her body and also scratched her causing immense injury to her. On her father's arrival in the evening after office hours, her father was taken aback to see injury marks with blood clots on her body and he immediately took her to Victoria hospital for the necessary treatment. After these incidents, fearing safety to herself and her child Disha, she refused to go back to her marital house. She state that on 2nd January 2010, our neighbours who are close to her family came to know of all these incidents and in a bid to patch up the issues and ensure that both she and the respondent No.1 live harmoniously rang up to talk to the respondent No.2 and requested him to advise his son and sort out the issues and take his daughter-in-law and child to their house and live there harmoniously and happily. But he respondent No.1 and 2 had approached sub- inspector of police, Bannerghatta police station to a lodge a false allegation against her and her family. The sub-inspector of Bannerghatta police station advised them to amicable settle the issue since this was a family matter and asked them to bring them also to counsel. Accordingly, her parents went to Bannerghata police station on 04-01-2010 at about 7.00 p.m. where both the families were counseled by the sub-inspector of Bannerghatta police station. Even his efforts went in vain because respondent No.1 and 2 refused to accept and insisted that her parents should given an apology letter to them for no reason and this they asked only with the sole intention of humiliating her father and also to cause pain to her. She did not want her father to give any such apology letter as this would only aggravate the difficult position she was in, in the respondents' house as they would use this to further cause mental and physical torture to her. And also this was no way to amend any problems and lead a happy married life. But this entire incident caused her a lot of mental disturbance. She state that after this the respondent No.1 lodged a written complaint with all false allegations against her parents and brother dating the same as 30th December 2009 and 2nd January 2010 for which he had also taken her signature by force well in Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141608679/ 7 advance. She was shocked to see that the respondent No.1 would stoop to such a low level as to take her signature and the same against her and her parents. She stated that respondent No.1 has got issued an undated legal notice to her, demanding mutual consent divorce through his counsel and the same was received by her on 25-01-2010 for which she got a reply sent on 06-02-2010. She has borne the harassment and torture silently only with the intention of making the marriage work and for the future of the child Disha though the violence caused by the respondents was too difficult to put up with, but the respondent No.1 has decided to wreck the marriage. She state that due to the continued harassment and threats heaped by the respondents, they are also constrained to lodge a complaint against the respondent No.1 to 3 U/s.498(A), 324, 120B, 506B, 307, 420,114 of IPC R/w. Sec.3 & 4 of D.P. Act in Crime No.44/10 on 27-01-2010, in the Bannerghatta police station wherein the police have also filed a charge sheet after investigation. She state that on 22-02-2010, the respondent No.1 has filed a petition for divorce on false allegations and accusations against her in M.C. No.574/10. Hence the accompanying application. 3. After registration of the case, summons was issued to the respondent and they appeared through their counsel and filed detailed statement of objection denying each and every allegations made against them. 4. In order to substantiate their respective contentions, the petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20. The respondents were given sufficient opportunity to conduct the cross-examination of P.W.1, but the respondents have failed to cross-examine the said petitioner. Hence the cross-examination of P.W.1 was taken as nil. The respondents have not led their evidence. Hence the respondents evidence is taken as nil.
texts.arguments: She state that a) The respondents are threatening her forcing her to withdraw the complaint filed by her against them or else they will put an end to her life and life of her daughter infant Disha. If their attempt in putting an end to their lives failed, they would ensure that they would also snatch and take away the child from her custody. On account of which, she is constrained to approach this Hon'ble Court for protection against the respondents. b) She is staying in her parents' house after she was forced to come out of the marital home. She do not have any roof of her own to stay anywhere in Bangalore whereas the respondent No.1 has a own house at Priyadarshni Farm house No.3 Pillaganahalli cross, Gottigere post, Bannergughatta road, Bangalore - 560 083. He also has a substantial income with which he can provide for both her daughter and her which he is duty bound to do. Hence she has approached this Hon'ble Court for protection by way of residence order against the respondent No.1. c) The respondent No.1 is not providing any maintenance to her and her daughter Disha right from the day she was forced out of the marital home and also never bothered about their well being at any point of time nor enquired about her or her daughter's well being leave alone maintain them. She do not want to be a burden to her family members any more as her parents have incurred huge expenses during her marriage and after her marriage which has crossed more than thirty lakh. The respondent had graduation in B.E. degree in environmental engineering and also a post graduate holder in finance and entrepreneurship and he is working as educational management consultant on his proprietorship concern and also he is working as a guest faulty at various business schools in Mumbai (Affiliated under Mumbai university). In this background his monthly earnings more than Rs.2,00,000/-. Apart from that he runs a 24 hours helpline coaching for students and earns not less than seventy five thousand to one lakh per month. The respondent No.1 does not have any dependents upon him as the respondent No.2 is a retired from ministry of defence and getting his pension whereas the respondent No.3 has her own agricultural source of income. Whereas she is unemployed and do not have any source of income. She is totally dependent upon her parents for everything for herself and for her child. She is also producing the tabulation about the expenses for leading a life commensurate with the standard of living of the respondent No.1. She has a right to lead a life in consonance with the life led by the respondents' standard of living and the life she is Smt. R. Chandana vs )Sri H. Manjunath on 3 January, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141608679/ 8 used to. Hence she has approached this Hon'ble Court for protection by way of monetary relief of Rs.50,000/- p.m. for herself and Rs.25,000/- towards her daughter. d) The respondents harassed and tortured her by demanding more dowry and made her life and her child's life a hell for no fault of ours. Hence she has approached this Hon'ble Court for compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/-. She state that she has tried to do everything possible to ensure that the respondents mend their ways in order to lead a peaceful life. Till this day, the respondents have not changed even a bit but continues to cause violence to her and her family members. But even as late as on 09-02-2011. the respondents have sent people who have been threatening them of dire consequences if she do not accept his terms and agree to divorce threatening the lives of her daughter, her siblings, her parents and her well wishes which forced her to file a complaint before the Chandra Layout police station on 11-02-2011 vide Cmis. No.59/11, now with no other alternative, she has been forced to approach this court for relief. She state that she has been subjected to severe acts of domestic violence by way of physical, emotional, verbal financial abuse. She state that she will be put to great hardship if the accompanying application is not allowed. On the other hand no such prejudice will be caused to the respondents if the accompanying application is allowed.
